question.text: How well must a driver know signs, signals and road markings?

answer.text: Every driver must know signs, signals and road markings well enough to recognize them instantly and to obey regulatory signs without hesitating.

teaching.text: Recognizing signs, signals and markings at a glance lets you obey regulatory signs right away, without hesitating. Remember: know them instantly, obey them.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every driver must know signs, signals and road markings well enough to recognize them instantly and to obey regulatory signs without hesitating.

question.text: Why do modern signs use more symbols and pictures?

answer.text: Signs now use more symbols and pictures because they can be recognized faster at higher speeds and from farther away.

teaching.text: Symbols and pictures can be read faster at higher speeds and from farther away than words. Remember: symbols read faster, farther.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Signs now use more symbols and pictures because they can be recognized faster at higher speeds and from farther away.

question.text: What do a sign's shape and color tell you?

answer.text: A sign's shape and its color are both coded to the kind of message it carries, so learn shapes and colors as well as individual signs.

teaching.text: Shape and color both code a sign's message, so learning them tells you the sign's type before you can read it. Remember: shape and color carry meaning.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A sign's shape and its color are both coded to the kind of message it carries, so learn shapes and colors as well as individual signs.

question.text: What are the three types of traffic signs?

answer.text: Traffic signs fall into three types by function: regulatory, warning, and information or guide signs.

teaching.text: Signs come in three types by function: regulatory, warning, and information or guide. Remember: regulatory, warning, guide.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Traffic signs fall into three types by function: regulatory, warning, and information or guide signs.

question.text: What do regulatory signs do, what colors are they, and must you obey them?

answer.text: Regulatory signs control how traffic moves, are black and white unless shown in their actual color, and must be obeyed.

teaching.text: Regulatory signs control how traffic moves, are black and white unless shown in their true color, and must be obeyed. Remember: regulatory means must obey.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Regulatory signs control how traffic moves, are black and white unless shown in their actual color, and must be obeyed.

question.text: At a four-way stop, which vehicle may go first?

answer.text: At a four-way stop, vehicles leave in the order they arrived, so the first one to come to a complete stop is the first one allowed to go.

teaching.text: Four-way stops run on arrival order: whoever stops completely first goes first. Remember: first to stop, first to go.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a four-way stop, vehicles leave in the order they arrived, so the first one to come to a complete stop is the first one allowed to go.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: first to stop, first to go

question.text: At a four-way stop, who goes first when vehicles arrive at the same moment?

answer.text: When two or more vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same moment, the one farthest to the right goes first.

teaching.text: When vehicles reach a four-way stop together, the one farthest to the right takes the first turn. Remember: tie goes to the right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When two or more vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same moment, the one farthest to the right goes first.

question.text: What should you do even when it is your turn at a four-way stop?

answer.text: Even when it is your turn at a four-way stop, wait at least a few seconds to be sure no one else starts into the intersection, because many drivers ignore the rule.

teaching.text: Even on your turn, give it a few seconds to make sure nobody else is pulling into the intersection. Remember: your turn? still look.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Even when it is your turn at a four-way stop, wait at least a few seconds to be sure no one else starts into the intersection, because many drivers ignore the rule.

question.text: What does a YIELD sign tell you to do?

answer.text: A YIELD sign tells you to slow down so you can give the right of way to pedestrians crossing and to vehicles on the intersecting road.

teaching.text: YIELD means slow down so pedestrians crossing and traffic on the intersecting road get the right of way. Remember: slow and give way.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A YIELD sign tells you to slow down so you can give the right of way to pedestrians crossing and to vehicles on the intersecting road.

question.text: What does a white-on-red regulatory sign about a one-way road or ramp warn?

answer.text: A white-on-red regulatory sign warns that you are heading onto a one-way highway or ramp from the wrong direction.

teaching.text: The white-on-red warning means you are heading onto a one-way highway or ramp from the wrong direction. Remember: wrong way, turn back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A white-on-red regulatory sign warns that you are heading onto a one-way highway or ramp from the wrong direction.

question.text: What does the sign marking a one-way road with oncoming traffic tell you?

answer.text: Another regulatory sign marks a one-way roadway whose traffic is coming toward you, and you may not enter it at that point.

teaching.text: Where a one-way road's traffic comes toward you, a regulatory sign tells you not to enter at that point. Remember: do not enter here.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Another regulatory sign marks a one-way roadway whose traffic is coming toward you, and you may not enter it at that point.

question.text: What does the railroad regulatory sign tell you to do?

answer.text: The railroad regulatory sign means approach with caution and make sure every track is clear before you cross.

teaching.text: The railroad regulatory sign calls for caution and a check that every track is clear before you cross. Remember: every track clear first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The railroad regulatory sign means approach with caution and make sure every track is clear before you cross.

question.text: What does a no-left-turn sign mean?

answer.text: A no-left-turn sign means you may not turn left at that intersection.

teaching.text: A no-left-turn sign bans left turns at that intersection, so plan another route if you need to go left. Remember: no left at this corner.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A no-left-turn sign means you may not turn left at that intersection.

question.text: May you park under a no-parking sign if you stay in the car?

answer.text: Under a no-parking sign you may not park in the area even if you remain inside the car.

teaching.text: Staying in the car does not make it legal to park under a no-parking sign. Remember: no parking, even sitting inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Under a no-parking sign you may not park in the area even if you remain inside the car.

question.text: When may a vehicle park in a space reserved for the physically handicapped?

answer.text: You may not park in a space reserved for the physically handicapped, on public or private property, unless a handicapped person drives or directs the vehicle and it visibly shows the handicapped sticker.

teaching.text: A reserved space needs a handicapped driver or director and a visible sticker, on public or private property. Remember: qualifying driver plus visible sticker.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may not park in a space reserved for the physically handicapped, on public or private property, unless a handicapped person drives or directs the vehicle and it visibly shows the handicapped sticker.

question.text: When may you stop where an EMERGENCY STOPPING ONLY sign is posted?

answer.text: An EMERGENCY STOPPING ONLY sign allows stopping only for real emergencies.

teaching.text: EMERGENCY STOPPING ONLY allows a stop only for a real emergency. Remember: real emergencies only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An EMERGENCY STOPPING ONLY sign allows stopping only for real emergencies.

question.text: What does a posted speed limit mean, for example SPEED LIMIT thirty?

answer.text: A posted speed limit is the speed allowed under normal conditions, and a sign reading SPEED LIMIT thirty means thirty miles an hour is the top speed in that area.

teaching.text: A posted limit is for normal conditions, so SPEED LIMIT thirty means thirty miles an hour is the top speed there. Remember: top speed in normal conditions.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A posted speed limit is the speed allowed under normal conditions, and a sign reading SPEED LIMIT thirty means thirty miles an hour is the top speed in that area.

question.text: What do signs posting both a maximum and a minimum speed tell you, and where do minimums usually appear?

answer.text: Some signs post both a maximum and a minimum speed for a stretch of highway, and minimum limits usually appear on freeways and other controlled-access highways.

teaching.text: Some stretches post a minimum as well as a maximum speed, mostly freeways and other controlled-access highways. Remember: minimums mostly on freeways.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Some signs post both a maximum and a minimum speed for a stretch of highway, and minimum limits usually appear on freeways and other controlled-access highways.

question.text: When does a school-zone speed limit apply?

answer.text: A school-zone speed limit applies during the hours the sign shows, and it may also be displayed on a lighted sign with flashing amber lights.

teaching.text: School-zone limits apply during the hours on the sign, sometimes shown with flashing amber lights. Remember: school hours or flashing amber.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A school-zone speed limit applies during the hours the sign shows, and it may also be displayed on a lighted sign with flashing amber lights.

question.text: What does a LEFT LANE MUST TURN LEFT sign mean?

answer.text: A LEFT LANE MUST TURN LEFT sign means traffic in the left lane has to turn left at the intersection ahead.

teaching.text: LEFT LANE MUST TURN LEFT means the left lane has to turn left at the intersection ahead. Remember: left lane turns left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A LEFT LANE MUST TURN LEFT sign means traffic in the left lane has to turn left at the intersection ahead.

question.text: What does a NO TURNS sign mean?

answer.text: A NO TURNS sign means you may turn neither right nor left at that intersection.

teaching.text: NO TURNS bans both right and left turns at that intersection. Remember: no right, no left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A NO TURNS sign means you may turn neither right nor left at that intersection.

question.text: What does one regulatory sign mark about passing?

answer.text: One regulatory sign marks where a no-passing zone begins.

teaching.text: One regulatory sign marks the point where a no-passing zone begins. Remember: start of no passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: One regulatory sign marks where a no-passing zone begins.

question.text: What does a NO TURN ON RED sign mean at a signal?

answer.text: Where a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted at a signal-controlled intersection, you may not turn right or left on a red light.

teaching.text: Where NO TURN ON RED is posted at a signal, neither right nor left turns are allowed on a red light. Remember: red means wait, no turns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Where a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted at a signal-controlled intersection, you may not turn right or left on a red light.

question.text: What does the regulatory sign telling you not to drive to its left require?

answer.text: One regulatory sign tells you not to drive to the left of it.

teaching.text: One regulatory sign tells you not to drive to its left, so keep to its right. Remember: keep to its right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: One regulatory sign tells you not to drive to the left of it.

question.text: What can a lane-use sign require of the right lane and the lane beside it?

answer.text: A lane-use sign can require the right lane to turn right while the lane beside it may either turn right or go straight.

teaching.text: A lane-use sign can make the right lane turn right while the lane beside it turns right or goes straight. Remember: right lane turns, next chooses.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A lane-use sign can require the right lane to turn right while the lane beside it may either turn right or go straight.

question.text: Where are double right turns allowed?

answer.text: Double right turns are allowed only at intersections signed for them; at unsigned intersections the normal right-turn rules apply.

teaching.text: Two lanes may turn right only where signs allow it; elsewhere the normal right-turn rules apply. Remember: double right only where signed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Double right turns are allowed only at intersections signed for them; at unsigned intersections the normal right-turn rules apply.

question.text: What does a one-way arrow sign mean?

answer.text: A one-way arrow sign means you may travel only in the direction the arrow points.

teaching.text: A one-way arrow sign limits you to the direction the arrow points. Remember: follow the arrow only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A one-way arrow sign means you may travel only in the direction the arrow points.

question.text: What colors are warning signs and construction warning signs?

answer.text: Warning signs are black on yellow, except construction-area warning signs, which are black on orange, and they warn of hazards that call for extra caution.

teaching.text: Ordinary warning signs are black on yellow, construction warnings are black on orange, and both call for extra caution. Remember: yellow warns, orange works.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Warning signs are black on yellow, except construction-area warning signs, which are black on orange, and they warn of hazards that call for extra caution.

question.text: What does fluorescent yellow on a sign mark?

answer.text: Fluorescent yellow on a sign marks pedestrian crossings and school zones.

teaching.text: Fluorescent yellow is used for pedestrian crossings and school zones. Remember: bright yellow for walkers, schools.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Fluorescent yellow on a sign marks pedestrian crossings and school zones.

question.text: What shape are most warning signs?

answer.text: Most warning signs are diamond shaped, though there are some exceptions.

teaching.text: Most warning signs are diamonds, though a few have other shapes. Remember: diamond means warning.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Most warning signs are diamond shaped, though there are some exceptions.

question.text: How do the three warning color schemes differ?

answer.text: Ordinary warning signs are black on yellow, construction warning signs are black on orange, and fluorescent yellow is kept for pedestrian crossings and school zones.

teaching.text: Black on yellow is an ordinary warning, black on orange a construction warning, and fluorescent yellow a crossing or school zone. Remember: yellow, orange, fluorescent.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Ordinary warning signs are black on yellow, construction warning signs are black on orange, and fluorescent yellow is kept for pedestrian crossings and school zones.

question.text: What do curve warning signs tell you?

answer.text: Curve warning signs tell you of a sharp left turn, a curve to the right, a gradual curve right then left, or a winding road ahead.

teaching.text: Curve warnings show a sharp left, a right curve, a reverse curve or a winding road ahead. Remember: curves and winding road ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Curve warning signs tell you of a sharp left turn, a curve to the right, a gradual curve right then left, or a winding road ahead.

question.text: What do side-road warning signs show?

answer.text: Side-road warning signs show that a side road joins the highway ahead, either from the right or at an angle.

teaching.text: Side-road warnings show a road joining the highway ahead from the right or at an angle. Remember: side road joins ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Side-road warning signs show that a side road joins the highway ahead, either from the right or at an angle.

question.text: What does a BUMP sign tell you?

answer.text: A BUMP sign warns of a bump ahead and tells you to slow down.

teaching.text: A BUMP sign means a bump lies ahead in the road, so slow down before you reach it. Remember: bump ahead, slow down.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A BUMP sign warns of a bump ahead and tells you to slow down.

question.text: What does the warning sign for a road that does not continue straight mean?

answer.text: One warning sign means the road does not continue straight, so you must turn right or left.

teaching.text: When a warning shows the road does not continue straight, plan to turn right or left. Remember: no straight, turn left or right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: One warning sign means the road does not continue straight, so you must turn right or left.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: no straight, turn left or right

question.text: What does a SOFT SHOULDER sign warn?

answer.text: A SOFT SHOULDER sign warns that the roadside is soft, so stay on the pavement.

teaching.text: A SOFT SHOULDER sign means the roadside is soft, so keep your wheels on the pavement. Remember: soft edge, stay on pavement.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A SOFT SHOULDER sign warns that the roadside is soft, so stay on the pavement.

question.text: What do the warnings for reverse sharp turns and a road ending both ways show?

answer.text: Other warning signs show a sharp left turn followed by a sharp right, or a road that ends ahead and turns both right and left.

teaching.text: Some warnings show a sharp left followed by a sharp right, or a road ending that turns both ways. Remember: sharp left then right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Other warning signs show a sharp left turn followed by a sharp right, or a road that ends ahead and turns both right and left.

question.text: What do arrow signs for sharp turns warn, and how are they set up?

answer.text: Arrow signs warn of a sharp turn or curve in the direction of the arrow and are normally set up in a series.

teaching.text: Arrow signs point the way of a sharp turn or curve and usually come in a series. Remember: arrows in a series.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Arrow signs warn of a sharp turn or curve in the direction of the arrow and are normally set up in a series.

question.text: What do ROAD NARROWS and PAVEMENT NARROWS signs mean?

answer.text: A ROAD NARROWS sign means the road ahead is narrower than the one you are on, and a PAVEMENT NARROWS sign means the paved surface ahead is narrower.

teaching.text: ROAD NARROWS is about the whole road getting narrower; PAVEMENT NARROWS is about the paved surface. Remember: road or pavement narrows.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A ROAD NARROWS sign means the road ahead is narrower than the one you are on, and a PAVEMENT NARROWS sign means the paved surface ahead is narrower.

question.text: What does an island-ahead warning sign allow?

answer.text: An island-ahead warning sign means you may pass the island on either side.

teaching.text: An island-ahead sign means you may pass the island on either side. Remember: either side of the island.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An island-ahead warning sign means you may pass the island on either side.

question.text: What does a DIP sign tell you?

answer.text: A DIP sign warns of a dip in the road and tells you to slow down.

teaching.text: A DIP sign means the road dips ahead, so slow down before you reach the low spot. Remember: dip ahead, slow down.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A DIP sign warns of a dip in the road and tells you to slow down.

question.text: What does a ONE LANE BRIDGE sign mean?

answer.text: A ONE LANE BRIDGE sign means the bridge ahead has no room for you to meet or pass another car or truck.

teaching.text: A ONE LANE BRIDGE leaves no room to meet or pass another car or truck on it. Remember: no room to meet or pass.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A ONE LANE BRIDGE sign means the bridge ahead has no room for you to meet or pass another car or truck.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: no room to meet or pass

question.text: How do ROAD NARROWS, PAVEMENT NARROWS and ONE LANE BRIDGE differ?

answer.text: ROAD NARROWS refers to the whole road getting narrower, PAVEMENT NARROWS to the paved surface, and ONE LANE BRIDGE to a bridge too narrow to meet or pass.

teaching.text: Road narrows is the whole road, pavement narrows is the paved part, and a one lane bridge is too narrow to meet or pass. Remember: road, pavement, or bridge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: ROAD NARROWS refers to the whole road getting narrower, PAVEMENT NARROWS to the paved surface, and ONE LANE BRIDGE to a bridge too narrow to meet or pass.

question.text: What do STOP AHEAD and YIELD AHEAD signs warn?

answer.text: STOP AHEAD and YIELD AHEAD signs warn that a STOP sign or a YIELD sign is coming up.

teaching.text: STOP AHEAD and YIELD AHEAD tell you a STOP or YIELD sign is coming up. Remember: control coming up.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: STOP AHEAD and YIELD AHEAD signs warn that a STOP sign or a YIELD sign is coming up.

question.text: Where does the stop or yield actually happen after a STOP AHEAD or YIELD AHEAD sign?

answer.text: STOP AHEAD and YIELD AHEAD signs only warn that a control is coming; the stop or yield itself happens at the STOP or YIELD sign further on.

teaching.text: These signs only warn; you stop or yield at the STOP or YIELD sign further on. Remember: warning first, sign later.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: STOP AHEAD and YIELD AHEAD signs only warn that a control is coming; the stop or yield itself happens at the STOP or YIELD sign further on.

question.text: What does an advisory speed sign give you?

answer.text: An advisory speed sign gives the top safe speed for taking the turn ahead.

teaching.text: An advisory speed sign gives the top safe speed for the turn ahead, so slow to it before the turn. Remember: safe speed for the turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An advisory speed sign gives the top safe speed for taking the turn ahead.

question.text: What does a railroad-crossing-ahead warning sign tell you to do?

answer.text: A railroad-crossing-ahead warning sign means slow down, look carefully both ways and be ready to stop, since a train cannot stop quickly.

teaching.text: The railroad-crossing-ahead sign means slow down, look both ways and be ready to stop, because trains stop slowly. Remember: slow, look, ready to stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A railroad-crossing-ahead warning sign means slow down, look carefully both ways and be ready to stop, since a train cannot stop quickly.

question.text: What does a low-shoulder sign warn?

answer.text: A low-shoulder sign warns that the shoulder sits much lower than the road surface.

teaching.text: A low-shoulder sign means the shoulder sits well below the road surface. Remember: shoulder drops below road.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A low-shoulder sign warns that the shoulder sits much lower than the road surface.

question.text: What do truck-crossing and fire-station signs tell you?

answer.text: Truck-crossing and fire-station signs tell you to watch for trucks or fire trucks pulling onto the road.

teaching.text: Truck-crossing and fire-station signs mean watch for trucks or fire trucks pulling onto the road. Remember: watch for trucks entering.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Truck-crossing and fire-station signs tell you to watch for trucks or fire trucks pulling onto the road.

question.text: What do PAVEMENT ENDS and DEAD END signs mean?

answer.text: A PAVEMENT ENDS sign warns that the surface ahead turns to gravel or dirt, and a DEAD END sign means the street has no outlet.

teaching.text: PAVEMENT ENDS warns of gravel or dirt ahead, and DEAD END means the street has no outlet. Remember: gravel ahead or no outlet.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A PAVEMENT ENDS sign warns that the surface ahead turns to gravel or dirt, and a DEAD END sign means the street has no outlet.

question.text: What do lane-ends signs warn, and why come three in a series?

answer.text: Lane-ends signs warn that the number of lanes changes ahead, and the three signs come in a series as a repeated reminder to merge into the next lane.

teaching.text: Lane-ends signs come in a series of three to remind you to merge into the next lane. Remember: lane ends, merge over.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Lane-ends signs warn that the number of lanes changes ahead, and the three signs come in a series as a repeated reminder to merge into the next lane.

question.text: Where does the NO PASSING ZONE warning sign stand?

answer.text: The NO PASSING ZONE warning sign stands on the left side of a two-lane road to warn where a no-passing zone begins.

teaching.text: The no-passing warning stands on the left side of a two-lane road where the zone begins. Remember: left side, zone begins.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The NO PASSING ZONE warning sign stands on the left side of a two-lane road to warn where a no-passing zone begins.

question.text: Which side of a two-lane road should you look for the no-passing warning sign?

answer.text: The no-passing warning sign belongs on the left side of a two-lane road, at the point where the zone begins, so look left for it.

teaching.text: Look to the left side of a two-lane road for the no-passing warning sign. Remember: look left for no passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The no-passing warning sign belongs on the left side of a two-lane road, at the point where the zone begins, so look left for it.

question.text: What does a low-clearance sign mean?

answer.text: A low-clearance sign means vehicles or loads taller than the clearance shown cannot fit under the structure ahead.

teaching.text: Low clearance means anything taller than the posted clearance cannot fit under the structure ahead. Remember: too tall will not fit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A low-clearance sign means vehicles or loads taller than the clearance shown cannot fit under the structure ahead.

question.text: What does a two-way traffic sign tell you?

answer.text: A two-way traffic sign means you are leaving a separated one-way roadway for a two-way road, and it also reminds drivers they are on a two-way road.

teaching.text: A two-way traffic sign means a separated one-way roadway ends and two-way traffic begins. Remember: two-way traffic ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A two-way traffic sign means you are leaving a separated one-way roadway for a two-way road, and it also reminds drivers they are on a two-way road.

question.text: At a merge sign, what does a driver joining from the right do?

answer.text: At a merge sign, a driver joining from the right gives way to main-route traffic and uses the speed-change lane to blend in smoothly.

teaching.text: At a merge, the driver joining from the right gives way and uses the speed-change lane to blend in. Remember: joiner gives way, blends in.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a merge sign, a driver joining from the right gives way to main-route traffic and uses the speed-change lane to blend in smoothly.

question.text: Which road changes do other warning signs announce?

answer.text: Other warning signs announce a traffic signal ahead, a crossroad, a divided highway starting or ending, and a downhill grade.

teaching.text: Other warnings mark a signal ahead, a crossroad, a divided highway starting or ending, and a downhill grade. Remember: signal, crossroad, divided, downhill.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Other warning signs announce a traffic signal ahead, a crossroad, a divided highway starting or ending, and a downhill grade.

question.text: Which hazards do other warning signs flag?

answer.text: Warning signs also flag slippery-when-wet pavement, a narrow bridge, cattle crossings and deer crossings.

teaching.text: Watch for warnings about slippery wet pavement, narrow bridges, cattle crossings and deer. Remember: slick, narrow bridge, cattle, deer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Warning signs also flag slippery-when-wet pavement, a narrow bridge, cattle crossings and deer crossings.

question.text: What does a pedestrian-crossing sign mean, and what must you do?

answer.text: A pedestrian-crossing sign marks a spot where people on foot often cross, not always at an intersection, and you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk while watching both sides.

teaching.text: Pedestrian crossings may be away from intersections, and you yield to anyone in the crosswalk. Remember: walkers cross, you yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A pedestrian-crossing sign marks a spot where people on foot often cross, not always at an intersection, and you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk while watching both sides.

question.text: What do school-crossing and school bus stop signs tell you?

answer.text: A school-crossing sign means slow down and watch for children crossing, and a separate sign warns of a school bus stop ahead.

teaching.text: Near a school crossing slow down for children, and expect a sign warning of a school bus stop. Remember: slow for children.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A school-crossing sign means slow down and watch for children crossing, and a separate sign warns of a school bus stop ahead.

question.text: In what colors may bicycle, pedestrian and school crossing signs appear?

answer.text: Bicycle, pedestrian and school crossing signs may appear in either their older or their current colors.

teaching.text: Crossing signs for bicycles, pedestrians and schools may be in older or current colors. Remember: old or new colors.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Bicycle, pedestrian and school crossing signs may appear in either their older or their current colors.

question.text: What does one bicycle sign state about passing a cyclist?

answer.text: One bicycle sign states that a three foot minimum clearance is required when passing a cyclist.

teaching.text: The bicycle sign states a three-foot minimum clearance when passing a cyclist. Remember: three feet to pass.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: One bicycle sign states that a three foot minimum clearance is required when passing a cyclist.

question.text: What does another bicycle sign tell drivers about a narrow lane?

answer.text: Another sign tells drivers that a cyclist may use the full lane when the travel lane is narrow.

teaching.text: Where the lane is narrow, a sign may tell you a cyclist can use the full lane. Remember: narrow lane, full lane bike.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Another sign tells drivers that a cyclist may use the full lane when the travel lane is narrow.

question.text: What do sharrows tell road users?

answer.text: Shared lane markings, called sharrows, tell road users that people on bicycles may be riding in the travel lane.

teaching.text: Sharrows on the pavement mean people on bicycles may be riding in the travel lane. Remember: shared lane, bikes inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Shared lane markings, called sharrows, tell road users that people on bicycles may be riding in the travel lane.

question.text: What does a ROAD CONSTRUCTION sign mean for you?

answer.text: A ROAD CONSTRUCTION sign means you are entering a work area, so watch for a flagman, one-way traffic, other signs or obstructions, go carefully and follow instructions.

teaching.text: A ROAD CONSTRUCTION sign means a work area: watch for flaggers, one-way traffic and obstructions, and follow instructions. Remember: work zone, watch and obey.

question.text: What other work-zone hazards do signs warn of?

answer.text: Work-zone signs also warn of a flagman ahead, workers in or near the road, and mowing equipment ahead.

question.text: What do large flashing or sequencing arrow panels in work zones do?

answer.text: Large flashing or sequencing arrow panels may be used in work zones by day and night to steer drivers into certain lanes and show that part of the road ahead is closed.
